title: Fail-safe Orchestra: KPI Decibel & Activation Canvas
content:
Purpose: This working canvas defines a compact, signal-driven launch orchestration that we call the 'Fail-safe Orchestra'. Goal is to produce a lightweight KPI signalboard (KPI Decibel) plus an activation checklist that can be run by on-call + product ops for pilot -> full launch flows.

Scope: applies to product ops-managed feature rollouts (hosted API + Dedicated beta). Focus on the first 72h post-traffic ramp and ongoing 30d health signals. Not a replacement for incident postmortems or engineering-level runbooks.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Canary traffic will be throttled via traffic lanes in Console (route: feature-x-canary).
- Dedicated capacity commitments must be validated 48h before full ramp.
- QA contract: regression eval suite must pass baseline prompts (eval-suite v2.1).

Quick summary for commanders:
- Primary commander: Maya Chen (product-ops). Secondary: Omar Patel (SRE liaison).
- Go/no-go: any Tier 1 SLA breach or sustained KPI Decibel > 7 for >30m requires rollback to previous traffic split.
- Quiet mode: use the quiet-launch checklist (section below) for low-visibility pilots.

KPI Decibel (single-pane signal model) — concept:
- Combine discrete metrics into a decibel-like score 0..10 where higher = louder/worse. Each metric maps to 0..10 by thresholding; weighted sum normalized. Designed for quick human interpretation on the runbook console.

KPI table (human-readable):
KPI | Source | Unit | Target | Alert threshold | Weight | Owner
- API latency (p50/p95) | telemetry.apiroute | ms | p95 < 450ms | p95 >= 650ms => +2 decibel | 3 | Ben Huang
- Error rate (500s) | telemetry.errors | % | <0.2% | >=0.5% => +3 decibel | 3 | Ben Huang
- Token cost / 1k | billing.usage | $ | <= $3/1k | >= $6/1k => +1 decibel | 1 | Finance (linked)
- Quality regression (eval-set) | eval.compare | delta F1 / percent | delta >= -2% => alarm | delta <= -5% => +4 decibel | 2 | Lucia Gomez
- KV cache hit rate | runtime.cache | % | >= 85% | < 70% => +1 decibel | 1 | Eng - Serving Runtime
- Throughput saturation | infra.queue | requests/s | headroom >= 20% | headroom < 5% => +2 decibel | 2 | SRE

Decibel scoring examples:
- Green: total <= 2 (quiet), Yellow: 2.1 - 5, Orange: 5.1 - 7, Red: >7 => escalate to incident commander and consider rollback.

Runbook triggers (what to do by decibel level):
- 0..2 (quiet): log and monitor, no action.
- 2.1..5 (watch): open a triage note in Confluence (template ID: launch-triage-v1). Assign owner in Slack channel #launch-ops.
- 5.1..7 (action): spin up dedicated fallback model route (model: small-latency-variant) and redirect 30% traffic. Start 15m cadence updates.
- >7 (commit): full rollback to previous rollout percentage within 10m, page SRE, engage exec on-call.

Activation checklist (pilot -> scale):
- Pre-activation (T-72h):
  - [ ] Confirm dedicated capacity reservation (infra ticket JIRA-9012).
  - [ ] Run regression eval suite and attach results to Confluence note.
  - [ ] Run smoke tests: latency, embedding correctness, streaming stability.
  - [ ] Confirm alerting endpoints + escalation policy in PagerDuty.
- Activation window (T-30m -> T+72h):
  - [ ] Set initial traffic split: 1% -> 5% (pilot) as per traffic matrix.
  - [ ] Enable KPI Decibel dashboard; confirm data sources refresh every 30s.
  - [ ] Inform CS leads + 1st cohort customers via email stub.
  - [ ] Post kickoff note in #launch-ops with baseline metrics snapshot.
- Post-activation (T+72h -> T+30d):
  - [ ] Run daily quality evals and track regression deltas.
  - [ ] Review cost per 1k tokens vs forecast (finance).
  - [ ] Schedule retro and accelerate to next ramp if signals green for 72h.

Heatmap snapshots to produce (for daily digest):
- Row headers: latency, errors, quality, cost, cache_hit, saturation. Columns: T-0, T+6h, T+24h, T+72h. Use red/orange/yellow/green encoding and highlight trending direction.

Owner responsibilities (short):
- Product-ops (Maya): command and coordinate, runbook updates, stakeholder comms.
- SRE (Omar): infra headroom, rollback procedures, autoscale checks.
- Serving runtime (Eng): cache tuning, batching knobs, model-variant readiness.
- Monitoring (Ben): dashboard config, alert tuning, KPI Decibel implementation.
- Applied ML (Lucia): quality evals, prompt set triage, model variant mapping.

Urgent decision matrix (quick):
- High latency + rising error rate: action level => route to latency optimized variant, reduce batch sizes, if persists >30m => rollback.
- Low cost but quality drop: action level => throttle new traffic, revert prompt/template change, engage Applied ML for immediate prompt rescoring.
- Sudden cost spike with no quality gain: watch => throttle non-essential routes, enable caching aggressively.

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- (TODO) Formalize metric weights and publish math in Confluence (owner: Ben).
- (Question) Do we include embedding throughput in Decibel or separate 'economics' panel? (rec: separate).
- (TODO) Wire the Decibel alerts into PagerDuty with low-noise escalation for night hours.

Appendix: quick links and templates:
- Confluence triage template: https://confluence.redwoodinternal/launch-triage-v1
- PagerDuty escalation plan (pilot): PD-PLAN-42
- Traffic matrix CSV: /sheets/activation-traffic-matrix-v3.csv (drive)
- Postmortem template: https://confluence.redwoodinternal/postmortem-template

Notes to self / rubrics (informal):
- Keep the Decibel simple — human operators should be able to eyeball and say "roll forward" vs "roll back" without parsing charts.
- Prefer automated fallback routes vs manual code changes for fastest mitigation.
- This doc is the team working draft; will convert to formal playbook after 2 successful pilots.

Version history (working):
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Maya).
- 2025-12-02: added Decibel thresholds & owners (Ben, Lucia).
- 2026-01-10: added heatmap snapshot cadence and decision matrix (Omar).

End of canvas.
